## $r^2$-exact $x_1$ maps on spherical-polar grids (`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`) {#sec-ch05-x1cent}

### Summary

A finite-volume cell on a spherical-polar grid holds the $r^2$ mean of a quantity, whose centroid sits
$\Delta x_1^2/(6r^{\mathrm m}_i)$ above the mid-radius $r^{\mathrm m}_i$. Every $x_1$ cell-to-face map of the solver, from the WENO weights to the
scan and the six-face cell pressure, is a formula for plain means. Fed $r^2$ means they are off by $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$: the face
values, the scan step, and the pressure force, whose plain difference balances gravity only against the wrong scan.
The switch converts the inputs of the maps, for the maps only, to plain means with a five-cell stencil exact to degree
4, and makes the radial pressure force the $r^2$ mean of the gradient of a quintic through six face pressures. The
reference on plain means is then the Cartesian one, and the switch implies `SNAP_WB_REF4` so that it is fourth order.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Feeds every $x_1$ map plain means instead of $r^2$ means, and makes the pressure source exact, @eq-ch05-x1cent-source.

**Data.** Reads the $r^2$ means and the face pressures; gives plain means to the $x_1$ maps and $S_i$ to the momentum source.

**Placement.** The $x_1$ sweep of `HydroImpl::forward` and `SphericalPolarImpl::forward`, every RK stage.

**Activation.** Environment variable `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, default off; acts on `spherical-polar`; implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Rest exact for densities of degree $\le4$; ratios of means keep $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ (@sec-ch05-oneoverr).

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch05-x1cent-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\langle q\rangle_i$ the $r^2$ mean and $\overline q_i$ the plain mean of cell $i$; $r^{\mathrm m}_i$ [m] the
mid-radius and $\Delta$ [m] the width $\Delta x_{1,i}$; $x$ [-] the local coordinate; $c_{i,l}$ [-] the conversion
weights and $c^S_{i,l}$ [m$^{-1}$] the source weights over the window starting at cell or face $i_0$, offset $l$;
$d_{\mathrm{mon}}$ the monomial degree; $\tilde p$ [Pa] the quintic through six face pressures; $S_i$ [Pa m$^{-1}$] the radial
pressure source. $\delta_i$[^rg-929a9e6df954], $A_{i\pm1/2}$[^rg-4cb11b837953], $V_i$[^rg-928038c8e04b], $p^{*}$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

On Cartesian blocks the switch only implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`; on cubed-sphere blocks it does nothing (their $x_{1v}$ is
the mid-radius). `balance_column` balances only a column declared Cartesian under it.

*Aliases.* "the centroid switch"; legs (i)-(iii) in the comments of `x1_centroid.hpp`.

### Derivation

Units: $r$[^rg-2ecd0b8c12cb] and $\Delta x_1$ [m]; $A_{i\pm1/2}=r_{i\pm1/2}^2$ and $V_i=(r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3)/3$ are per unit solid angle, as the
code forms them. $\langle q\rangle_i=V_i^{-1}\int r^2q\,\mathrm{d}r$ is the $r^2$ mean, $\overline q_i=\Delta x_{1,i}^{-1}\int q\,\mathrm{d}r$ the plain
mean, and $x=(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)/\Delta x_{1,i}$ the local coordinate, with $r^{\mathrm m}_i=\tfrac12(r_{i-1/2}+r_{i+1/2})$ the mid-radius (appendix A $x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$[^rg-9f1279c76a64]). Re-written from the derivation note.[^ch05-x1c-note]

[^ch05-x1c-note]: `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274` §§1-5.

#### The defect

Write $r^{\mathrm m}_i=\tfrac12(r_{i-1/2}+r_{i+1/2})$ for the mid-radius and $\Delta=\Delta x_{1,i}$. Expanding $q$ about
$r^{\mathrm m}_i$, $q(r)=q+(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)\,\partial_1q+\tfrac12(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2\,\partial_1^2q+\tfrac16(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^3\,\partial_1^3q+\dots$,
with $q$ and its derivatives taken at $r^{\mathrm m}_i$, the two means need the moments of $r-r^{\mathrm m}_i$ on each
measure. With $\int r^2\,\mathrm dr=\Delta\big((r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2+\Delta^2/12\big)$ and
$\int(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)\,r^2\,\mathrm dr=r^{\mathrm m}_i\Delta^3/6$ over the cell,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_i &= \langle r-r^{\mathrm m}_i\rangle_i = \frac{r^{\mathrm m}_i\Delta^3/6}{\Delta\big((r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2+\Delta^2/12\big)}
 = \frac{2\Delta^2\,r^{\mathrm m}_i}{\Delta^2+12\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}
 = \frac{\Delta^2}{6r^{\mathrm m}_i}-\frac{\Delta^4}{72\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^3}+\cdots, \\
\langle (r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2\rangle_i &= \frac{\Delta^2}{12}+\frac{\Delta^4}{180\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}+\cdots,
\qquad \overline{(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}_i=\frac{\Delta^2}{12},\qquad \overline{(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)}_i=0,
\end{aligned}
$$

so that

$$
\langle q\rangle_i = \overline q_i + \delta_i\,\partial_1 q(r^{\mathrm m}_i)
+ \frac{\Delta^4}{240\,r^{\mathrm m}_i}\,\partial_1^3q + \frac{\Delta^4}{360\,(r^{\mathrm m}_i)^2}\,\partial_1^2q + O(\Delta^6),
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-defect}

$\delta_i$ being the centroid offset of appendix A (`[C18]`, exact). The second-moment difference gives the last term
and the third moment $\langle(r-r^{\mathrm m}_i)^3\rangle_i=\Delta^4/(40\,r^{\mathrm m}_i)+\dots$ the one before it, so the
remainder after $\delta_i\partial_1q$ is $O(\Delta x_1^4/r)$. Each uniform-measure map fed $\langle q\rangle$ is off by
$\delta_i\partial_1q=O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$; in particular the scan step becomes $g\Delta x_1\langle\rho\rangle$ instead of
$g\int\rho\,\mathrm{d}r=g\Delta x_1\overline\rho$, and the perturbation of a resting column is $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ instead of
a constant.

#### Plain means

For the $x_1$ maps only, each primitive row is replaced by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline q_i &= \sum_{l=0}^{4} c_{i,l}\,\langle q\rangle_{i_0+l}, \\
\sum_l c_{i,l}\,\langle x^{d_{\mathrm{mon}}}\rangle_{i_0+l} &= \overline{x^{d_{\mathrm{mon}}}}_i = \big(1,\ 0,\ \tfrac1{12},\ 0,\ \tfrac1{80}\big)_{d_{\mathrm{mon}}},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-conv}

for the monomial degrees $d_{\mathrm{mon}}=0..4$, window $i_0=\max(\mathrm{lo},\min(\mathrm{hi}-4,i-2))$, centred, inside the owned cells at a physical wall and inside the
array at a seam. The moments are integrated by four-point Gauss-Legendre, exact to degree 7 while every integrand has degree at most 6, and the $5\times5$ system
is solved once per block. The conversion is exact for degree 4 and not 5, on uniform and stretched grids and in the
wall windows, and its weights sum to 1 (`[C16]`). @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv is `x1_plain_mean_stencils`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_mean_stencils >}}).
Ghosts past a physical wall get the mirrored correction of the owned cells, odd for the normal velocity unless the
boundary is `outflow`, in
`x1_plain_means`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_means >}});
at a seam the outer ghosts' windows are off-centre, so their plain means are replaced by the neighbour's.

#### The pressure source

With $\tilde p$ the quintic through the six face pressures nearest cell $i$ (window over faces, one-sided at a wall,
reaching two faces past a seam), the radial pressure source is

$$
S_i = \frac{2}{V_i}\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r\,\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r = \sum_{l=0}^{5}c^S_{i,l}\,p^{*}_{i_0+l},
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-source}

and integration by parts gives the net pressure force. Since $\partial_r(r^2\tilde p)=2r\tilde p+r^2\partial_r\tilde p$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_iV_i = 2\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r\,\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r
&= \big[r^2\tilde p\big]_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} - \int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r^2\,\partial_r\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r \\
&= A_{i+1/2}p^{*}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{*}_{i-1/2} - \int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r^2\,\partial_r\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r ,
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second line uses that $\tilde p$ passes through both faces of the cell, $\tilde p(r_{i\pm1/2})=p^{*}_{i\pm1/2}$,
and $A_{i\pm1/2}=r_{i\pm1/2}^2$. Dividing by $V_i$,
$-(A_{i+1/2}p^{*}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{*}_{i-1/2})/V_i+S_i=-V_i^{-1}\int r^2\,\partial_r\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r$: the net pressure force is
the $r^2$ mean of $-\partial_r\tilde p$. A constant pressure gives $S_iV_i=A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}$ exactly, with $V_i$ in the
cube form of the cell volume (`[C17]`, both identities in exact rationals). @eq-ch05-x1cent-source is
`x1_pressure_source_stencils`
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_pressure_source_stencils >}}),
used in place of the plain difference by the branch that tests `exact_x1`
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}).
The hydrostatic mode takes the same operator (@sec-ch05-hsmode).

#### Rest balance

On a hydrostatic column of $r^2$ means: the conversion gives $\overline\rho$ to $O(\Delta x_1^6/r)$; the scan then gives the
exact face pressures plus one constant; the reference on plain means is the Cartesian fourth-order one; and the net
force $-V^{-1}\int r^2(\partial_r\tilde p+g\rho)\,\mathrm{d}r$ has the constant drop out. For a density of degree $\le4$ every step
is exact and the column is balanced exactly, which is the oracle of the test.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the conversion for degree 4, both source identities, rest for degree $\le4$. For a
smooth column the curvature part of the residual is $O(\Delta x_1^6/r)$; what remains is the truncation of the reference itself.
Ratios of means (the Favre velocity, $T=p/\rho$, $\chi$ inside $\mathsf F$) are not made exact (@sec-ch05-oneoverr); for the
velocity, `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` subtracts the covariance part (@sec-ch04-x1masscov).

*Why a resting column of $r^2$ means stays at rest.* Four steps, each a line of the code.

1. *The maps read plain means.* `HydroImpl::forward` hands `wx1 = x1_plain_means(...)` to `_hydro_ref_x1` and to the
   reconstruction, and the conserved state keeps its $r^2$ means: `wx1` is a separate tensor. Plain means are
   averages in $r$, so under the switch `HydroImpl::reset` gives the $x_1$ reconstruction of a spherical-polar block
   the per-face rows of the $r$ faces `x1f` on a keyed stretched $x_1$, and leaves it on its uniform weights
   otherwise; it does not use the volume-coordinate rows that `x1_row_faces` returns without the switch
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. *The seam ghosts are the neighbour's.* `_x1_ghost_rows(wx1, ...)` replaces the off-centre ghost windows, so a split
   column converts like one block.
3. *The source is the exact $r$-moment.* With the face pressures defined, `SphericalPolarImpl::forward` adds
   `x1_pressure_source` instead of the plain-difference correction, and its weights divide by the cube-form volume
   `(xf[i+1]^3 - xf[i]^3)/3` that `cell_volume()` uses, so a constant pressure exerts no force.
4. *The reference is then Cartesian.* On plain means the scan and @sec-ch05-wbref4 are the Cartesian operators, and
   the net force is the $r^2$ mean of $-(\partial_r\tilde p+g\rho)$, zero for degree $\le4$.

*Round-off.* The conversion is a five-term sum, so by the dot-product bound $\overline q_i$ carries at most
$5\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert c_{i,l}\rvert\max\lvert\langle q\rangle\rvert$ besides the rounding of the weights from
the $5\times5$ solve, which is not bounded here; for $\Delta\ll r$ the weights approach the plain fourth-order
ones and $\sum_l\lvert c_{i,l}\rvert$ stays of order 1. The pressure force is the source minus the flux divergence, two terms each of size about
$p/\Delta x_1$ (since $A/V\approx1/\Delta x_1$). For the constant-pressure identity of @eq-ch05-x1cent-source the
rounding count is, to first order with $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ per operation:

1. *The flux difference.* $(r_{i+1/2}^2p-r_{i-1/2}^2p)/V_i$ rounds the two squares and the two products, each by
   $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ of a term of size $r^2p/V_i\approx p/\Delta x_1$: at most $2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,p/\Delta x_1$. The
   subtraction and the division round the difference, of size $2p/r$, and add $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}p/r$.
2. *The source.* `apply` sums six products, so by the dot-product bound it carries at most
   $3\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_l\lvert c^S_{i,l}\rvert p$, of size $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}p/r$ since $c^S\sim 1/r$.
3. *The common volume.* $V_i$ divides both terms, so its rounding scales the net force, not the two large terms.
4. *Hence* $\lvert S_i-(A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2})p/V_i\rvert\le2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,p/\Delta x_1$ for $r\gg\Delta x_1$. A float64 port of
   `x1_pressure_source_stencils` measures at most $0.90\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,p/\Delta x_1$ at $r_0$ = 5, 60 and 1000
   (`derivation_check.py`, `XC-4`), inside it. In units of $g\rho$ the bound is $2\epsilon_{\mathrm m}H_p/\Delta x_1$, with
   $H_p=p/(\rho g)$ the pressure scale height.

The rest test's column ($\rho=1-0.3(r-r_0)$, $g=1$, $\Delta x_1=1/16$) has $H_p/\Delta x_1$ between 38 and 40, so the
bound is $1.8\times10^{-14}$ in units of $g\rho$; its rest forces with the switch, $0.86$ to $3.3\times10^{-14}$
(@tbl-ch05-x1cent-rest), include the rounding of the reconstruction, the Riemann flux and the gravity source as well.

**Not provided:** a round-off bound for that complete rest-force calculation; the operation count above
is limited to the constant-pressure flux/source identity and excludes those additional operations.

### Numerical method

The windows are shown in @fig-ch05-x1cent-window. In `HydroImpl::forward` the plain-mean view `wx1` is computed before the
reference, its seam ghost rows are taken from the neighbour, and the reconstruction and the reference read it; the
primitives themselves are unchanged. After the Riemann solve the two ghost face pressures each side of a seam are taken
from the neighbour, so the source window is the centred one-block window. Everything runs in every RK stage,
explicitly; the stencils are built once per block in double precision.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-x1cent-window
#| fig-cap: "The maps of `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, $x_1 = r$ to the right. Top: a radial cell, its mid-radius $r^{\\mathrm{m}}_i$ (dotted) and its $r^2$ centroid $x_{1v}$ (bluish-green line), to leading order $\\Delta x_1^2/(6r^{\\mathrm{m}}_i)$ [m] further out. Middle: the five-cell window that converts $r^2$ means to the plain mean of cell $i$, centred in the interior and one-sided at the wall (thick black line). Bottom: the six-face window of the pressure source (orange triangles), which reaches two faces past a seam (dashed reddish-purple line) into the neighbour's hatched ghost cells."
#| fig-alt: "A single wide cell with two vertical lines inside, below it a row of nine cells with brackets over five cells, and a third row of cells with a dashed seam and six triangles crossing it."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch05.figures.fig_x1cent_window import make_fig
```

### Code

**A minimal input.** The switch is an environment variable. It acts on a spherical-polar block with gravity along
$x_1$ and three ghost cells; the geometry of the rest test, trimmed:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `x2min`[^rg-014edceb12dd], `x2max`[^rg-375990ed62cb], `x3min`[^rg-0c4c6ec9886a], `x3max`[^rg-b76d566586e6], `nx2`[^rg-57b83d82009d], `nx3`[^rg-b072e4593cae], `integration`[^rg-9872a488778d], `tlim`[^rg-ddc90b088c91].
```yaml
geometry:
  type: spherical-polar
  bounds: {x1min: 5., x1max: 7., x2min: 1.4, x2max: 1.7, x3min: 0., x3max: 0.3}
  cells: {nx1: 32, nx2: 4, nx3: 4, nghost: 3}   # three ghost cells for the well-balanced reference check
boundary-condition:
  external: {x1-inner: reflecting, x1-outer: reflecting}
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -1.}
integration:
  tlim: 1.          # a short demonstration run, not the 900 s of the Straka deck
```

With these keys in a copy of `straka_single.yaml`, saved as `deck.yaml` in `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)), run

```bash
SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1 ./straka.release deck.yaml
```

This is a short demonstration run. The time step on this grid is about $1.6\times10^{-4}$, so `tlim: 1.` is about
6200 steps, half a minute on six CPU cores. Without the `tlim` line the copy keeps the deck's 900 s, which is several
hours.

A PyPI release of snapy has no such switch and ignores the variable without a message.

**What it refuses, and why.** Since the switch implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`, setup refuses $n_g<3$ with gravity on
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}), for the seam reason of @sec-ch05-wbref4. `balance_column` refuses
it with any geometry other than `"cartesian"`
({{< code src/hydro/balance_column.cpp balance_column >}}), because a ghost-free column does not model the conversion.
Not refused: on a block with fewer than five cells between its walls, or fewer than six faces for the source, the
stencils are marked unusable and the plain path runs ({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_mean_stencils >}}).

**The lines that implement @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv and @eq-ch05-x1cent-source.** In `x1_pressure_source_stencils`
each source weight is the Gauss sum of $r\,\ell_l$, $\ell_l$ the Lagrange basis of the six faces:

```cpp
for (int q = 0; q < 4; ++q) {
  double r = c + 0.5 * h * kGx[q];
  wt[j] += 0.5 * h * kGw[q] * r * lagrange(X, j, 0.5 * kGx[q]);
}
wt[j] *= 2. / vol;
```

and in `SphericalPolarImpl::forward` the source replaces the plain difference:

```cpp
if (exact_x1) {
  src1.slice(-1, si, ei) += x1_pressure_source(*x1src_, face_pressure1);
} else if (face_pressure1.defined()) {
```

`wt[j]` is $c^S_{i,l}$ with $l$ = `j`; the loop is the integral $\int r\tilde p\,\mathrm dr$ of @eq-ch05-x1cent-source over
the cell, and `2. / vol` its prefactor $2/V_i$. The conversion weights $c_{i,l}$ of @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv are the
solution `wgt = solve(M, rhs)` with `rhs` the plain moments $(1,0,\tfrac1{12},0,\tfrac1{80})$.

|--------|----------|----------|------|
| the switch | {{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}} | `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` | `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` |
| conversion stencils | {{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_mean_stencils >}} | `x1_plain_mean_stencils` | |
| conversion and mirrored ghosts | {{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_plain_means >}} | `x1_plain_means` | |
| source stencils | {{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_pressure_source_stencils >}} | `x1_pressure_source_stencils` | |
| plain-mean view and seam ghosts | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `x1_plain_means` | spherical-polar |
| ghost face pressures at a seam | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `_x1_ghost_rows` | |
| the source in the momentum equation | {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}} | `x1_pressure_source` | |
| ghost-row exchange | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_x1_ghost_rows >}} | `_x1_ghost_rows` | $x_1$ split |
| implies `SNAP_WB_REF4` | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}} | `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` | |

: Code map of `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`. {#tbl-ch05-x1cent-code}

1. `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` reads the environment once
   ({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}).
2. On a spherical-polar block `HydroImpl::forward` builds the view with `x1_plain_means` and exchanges its seam ghost
   rows with `_x1_ghost_rows`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
3. The reference and the reconstruction of @sec-ch05-wbx1 read the view, the reconstruction with the $r$-face rows on
   a keyed stretched $x_1$ (`plain`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}); `SNAP_WB_REF4` acts
   through `wb_ref4_enabled` (@sec-ch05-wbref4).
4. After the Riemann solve the face-pressure ghost rows are exchanged with `_x1_ghost_rows`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. `SphericalPolarImpl::forward` adds `x1_pressure_source` in place of the plain-difference correction
   ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}).

The ghost-depth check of @sec-ch05-wbref4 covers this switch, since it implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`; `balance_column` refuses
a non-Cartesian geometry under it. A block too thin for the stencils (`usable` false) keeps the plain path silently.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The switch does nothing on cubed-sphere grids. Under it `balance_column` balances only a column declared
`geometry='cartesian'`.
:::

1. **Ratios of means.** The Favre velocity, $T$ and $\chi$ are still treated as means (the velocity's covariance part is
   subtracted under `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE`); the $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ remainder
   is @sec-ch05-oneoverr.
2. **Cubed sphere.** Not implemented: the gnomonic grids store the mid-radius as $x_{1v}$ and would need the
   conversion with their own radial measure.
3. **The source copy differs from the code.** The copy of the derivation in the report's sources says the switch
   leaves the reference unchanged;[^ch05-x1c-copy] at the pin it implies `SNAP_WB_REF4` and seam ghosts are
   exchanged.
4. **Untested combinations.** See the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
